name: Hange-shashin-to (Kampo formula)
short: Case reports: severe drug-induced lung disease in 2 people with head and neck cancer; authors note rare cases including deaths. Overactive bladder pilot (29): adverse events mostly mild to moderate.
text: A 2025 report describes 2 people with head and neck cancer who were clinically diagnosed with severe drug-induced interstitial lung disease after taking hange-shashin-to for radiation-induced mucositis (the abstract does not give the route); reviewing the literature, the authors state that the formula is associated with a relatively low incidence of drug-induced interstitial lung disease, including some reports of death, and urge greater attention when prescribing it, especially for elderly patients with factors predisposing them to severe lung disease. In a 12-week single-arm pilot study in 29 people with overactive bladder who took the formula in addition to their bladder medicines, treatment-related adverse events were generally mild to moderate. In a placebo-controlled trial in 93 people with colorectal cancer who had developed chemotherapy-induced mouth sores (oral mucositis), no difference in other treatment toxicity was seen between the formula and placebo (the abstract does not give the route). No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
